task: finite-range electrolyte conductivity statistic, finite-time sampling error, and matched tracer-only baseline
prior_art_boundary: The Green-Kubo/Einstein-Helfand collective-conductivity identity and the self-only Nernst-Einstein approximation are established. No novelty or priority claim is made for the general role of ionic correlations. The results below are internal derivations for a selected channelized SSEP model; no material-specific validity is established.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For two independent periodic one-dimensional channels of L sites and spacing a, with N hard-core ions of charge +q in one channel and N ions of charge -q in the other, each particle-vacancy exchange occurring at rate gamma per active nearest-neighbor bond, let V=2 A L a and F be the total number of unlike neighboring occupancy pairs over the two channels. The finite product-canonical process is irreducible and reversible. Under stationarity, the total unwrapped charge displacement Q_t is a martingale with predictable bracket q^2 a^2 gamma integral_0^t F(eta_s) ds. Since E_pi F=4N(L-N)/(L-1), the one-dimensional EH conductivity is exactly sigma_L=beta q^2 a gamma N(L-N)/(A L(L-1)); if N/L tends to rho in (0,1), sigma tends to beta q^2 a gamma rho(1-rho)/A. The model-specific observable integral F is unbiased and conductivity-identifying when gamma and the other parameters are supplied.
claims.status: internally derived exact finite-state model theorem; proof in report; only small finite combinatoric checks run; no external proof review
claims.finite_check: work/agents/materials_energy/battery_transport/verify_cycle2.py enumerates canonical occupancy states for L=3..10 and checks active-bond means, telescoping drift, and conductivity prefactors. This is a finite diagnostic, not the proof.
claims.novelty_boundary: The EH/GK relation and NE diagonal restriction are established prior art. The local-activity statistic is derived for this SSEP generator only. No priority search for an equivalent model calculation was performed.
claims.costs: Analytic conductivity requires beta, q, a, A, gamma, L, and N. Event-driven estimation with R stationary replicas of duration t uses 2L occupancy bits plus counters, O(L) initialization, O(1) active-bond updates per event, and at most O(R gamma L t) accepted-hop event processing. No force-field or electronic-structure calculations are part of this Markov simulation. Machine energy was not measured.
claims.falsifier: An algebraic contradiction in the martingale bracket, canonical active-bond mean, or EH normalization would falsify the internal claim. For a real material, failure of the assumed local uniform-rate generator or a matched measured activity prediction inconsistent with independent collective conductivity rejects transfer of this mechanism.
claims.next_gate: For one named electrolyte, map local states and rates from a validated trajectory, estimate integrated active-bond time, then compare the prediction with independent EH/GK or bulk impedance at matched T, stoichiometry, phase, and geometry.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For the preceding model, start R independent trajectories from the product canonical stationary distribution, each of duration t. Set F=B_++B_-, mu_L=E_pi F=4N(L-N)/(L-1), c_L=beta q^2 a^2 gamma/(2V), and sigma_hat=c_L (Rt)^(-1) sum_r integral_0^t F(eta_s^r) ds. The SSEP spectral gap is lambda_L=2 gamma(1-cos(2 pi/L)); reversible covariance decay and 0<=F<=2L imply Var((Rt)^(-1) sum_r integral F ds)<=2L^2/(lambda_L R t). Therefore P(|sigma_hat-sigma_L|>=epsilon)<=2 c_L^2 L^2/(lambda_L R t epsilon^2), and P(|sigma_hat-sigma_L|>=eta sigma_L)<=2L^2/(lambda_L R t eta^2 mu_L^2).
claims.status: internally derived nonasymptotic Chebyshev guarantee conditional on stationary starts and the exact SSEP model; conservative bound, not an empirical error bar
claims.novelty_boundary: The spectral-gap identity is an established theorem by Caputo, Liggett, and Richthammer. The integrated-observable error inequality is derived here from stationary reversible covariance decay; no novelty or optimality claim is made.
claims.costs: A sufficient large-L exposure for relative tolerance eta and failure probability delta is Rt >= L^2/[32 pi^2 gamma delta eta^2 rho^2(1-rho)^2]. This bound uses exact stationary initialization; nonstationary initialization needs separate burn-in/bias accounting. Event processing cost is described in the report.
claims.falsifier: A violation under exact stationary SSEP sampling would contradict the covariance/gap derivation or indicate a normalization or implementation error. Nonstationary starts, finite-resolution missed hops, unknown gamma, or a non-SSEP material process fall outside the bound.
claims.next_gate: Implement independent stationary replicas for selected L,N and compare empirical activity-estimator errors to the stated loose bound before applying it to any measured material trajectory.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For the same finite ring/channel parameters, cyclic order preservation and the martingale of total particle displacement imply D_self,L=gamma a^2 (L-N)/(N(L-1)) for a tagged ion. For two signs with N ions each and total volume V=2ALa, the self-only Nernst-Einstein estimate is sigma_NE,L=beta q^2 gamma a (L-N)/(A L(L-1)), while sigma_L/sigma_NE,L=N. At fixed N/L tending to rho in (0,1), sigma_NE,L tends to zero whereas sigma_L tends to beta q^2 a gamma rho(1-rho)/A. The infinite-volume zero-tracer-diffusion conclusion is also consistent with the published one-dimensional nearest-neighbor SSEP tagged-particle t^(1/4) CLT and MSD of order t^(1/2).
claims.status: finite-ring tracer formula internally derived; thermodynamic contrast follows exactly from formulas; infinite-line subdiffusive behavior is independently source-reported
claims.novelty_boundary: Tracer subdiffusion in 1D SSEP and failure of self-only NE under correlations are established ideas. This is a model-specific exact finite-ring matched calculation. No real battery prediction or priority claim is made.
claims.costs: The matched NE calculation requires the same L,N,T and the long-time single-tag MSD; the collective estimator uses the local activity statistic or full charge displacement. Tracer data alone miss the active-bond/collective-current information in this model. Experimental comparison needs matched tracer and direct ionic conductivity measurements.
claims.falsifier: A contradiction of the cyclic-order displacement relation or finite-ring D formula would falsify the internal calculation. For nature, evidence that ions pass within the effective channel, interact across channels, have nonuniform/non-Markov rates, or show a collective conductivity inconsistent with the activity law rejects this model mechanism.
claims.next_gate: Test whether a specific one-dimensional or strongly channelized ionic material has the required order-preserving local dynamics; otherwise retain the result only as a mathematical counterexample to a locality-based universal NE claim.

global_unresolved: No molecular dynamics, kinetic Monte Carlo trajectory, electronic-structure calculation, or experiment was run; the finite script only enumerates static states and checks algebra.
No named battery electrolyte was parameterized, and no local activity statistic was measured in nature.
The model omits Coulomb interactions, solvent/framework motion, energetic disorder, polarization, and electronic leakage; transfer to a material is unvalidated.
The Chebyshev bound is conservative and assumes exact stationary starts and known gamma; no concentration-optimality claim is made.
No external mathematical audit or exhaustive source-priority search was performed.
